html:
An old Persian name for the lands north and east of Iran, beyond the Amu Darya: the steppes and oases of western Central Asia. The map uses it for the whole region in 1815.

In the Shahnameh of Ferdowsi, Turan is the land of Tur and the age-old enemy of Iran, and its king Afrasiab fights Iran's heroes for generations. Over time the name came to mean the land of the Turks.

In 1815 the region was no single state. It held three Uzbek-ruled states: the Emirate of Bukhara, the Khanate of Khiva and the Khanate of Kokand, each built on irrigated oases ringed by desert. Turkmen tribes held the deserts to the south, and the Kazakh hordes the steppe to the north, already drifting under Russian rule. Within sixty years Russia had conquered nearly all of it, starting in earnest when Russia took Tashkent in 1865.
